pages.lesson:
LESSON: SILENT READING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.3: Silent reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Silent reading. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read texts and passages silently 3 lessons focus for longer periods (15-20 minutes)
2. predict the meaning of unfamiliar words
3. answer comprehension questions from texts read e) develop an interest in reading texts for enjoyment spark that tells the same story ( a wedding ceremony)

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. read texts and passages silently 3 lessons focus for longer periods (15-20 minutes)
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to read texts and passages silently 3 lessons focus for longer periods (15-20 minutes). Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. predict the meaning of unfamiliar words
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to predict the meaning of unfamiliar words. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. answer comprehension questions from texts read e) develop an interest in reading texts for enjoyment spark that tells the same story ( a wedding ceremony)
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to answer comprehension questions from texts read e) develop an interest in reading texts for enjoyment spark that tells the same story ( a wedding ceremony). Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Silent reading.
2. Explain Silent reading to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Silent reading.
4. Show that you can: read texts and passages silently 3 lessons focus for longer periods (15-20 minutes)
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Silent reading. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Silent reading important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. read texts and passages silently 3 lessons focus for longer periods (15-20 minutes)
2. predict the meaning of unfamiliar words
3. answer comprehension questions from texts read e) develop an interest in reading texts for enjoyment spark that tells the same story ( a wedding ceremony)

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
